cmes.note: CME first seen to the W part way into the FOV of STEREO A COR2 following a real-time data gap that ended at 2026-11-12T01:53Z. The source may be related to some "flickering" seen beyond the WSW limb in STA EUVI after a real-time data gap ending at 2026-11-12T01:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to beyond-limb source and single coronagraph view.

cmes.note: Faint CME seen to NNW in early SOHO LASCO C2 coronagraph imagery and very faintly in early timestamps of GOES CCOR-1 but completely covered by an evening data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. Its source is most likely a faint prominence seen erupting on/behind the NNW limb starting at 2026-11-12T21:13Z, as seen to the NNW in GOES SUVI 304. Unfortunately, the source cannot be seen in STEREO A EUV imagery, since it is covered by the above mentioned data gap in STEREO A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to beyond-limb source and single coronagraph view, because of the data gap in STEREO A.

cmes.note: CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery and to the SSE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is not clear, but some faint dimming and moving field lines are seen to the far south in SDO AIA 171/193 imagery starting around 2026-11-12T17:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The leading edge of the CME is unclear, so this measurement is more approximate than usual and based on the fastest portion of the CME prior to it leaving the field of view of STEREO A COR2.

cmes.note: This CME is faintly visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 due to Earthshine starting 2026-11-13T03:45Z. The potential source may be an eruption with a small region of dimming and post-eruption arcades starting at 2026-11-13T00:21Z as best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery from Active Region 14575 (S09E50).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This measurement only uses one frame of available SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and is primarily based on STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: CME faintly visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is not clear, but may be some faint field line movement seen to the west in STEREO A COR2 EUV 195 imagery around 2026-11-13T08:00Z. Dimming is also seen to the south of the large coronal hole seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery as well. Moving/opening field lines are visible beyond the west limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA starting at 2026-11-13T08:27Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cmes.note: A faint messy front seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2 and later in C3 and GOES CCOR-1 as a messy fuzzy half-loop. There is also a much fainter loop seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph to the SW, but this loop in STEREO A COR2 seems to be starting much earlier (first seen ~13Z), so it is likely a different event.

A very small CME seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs, and in early timestamps of C3. The front is not clear in GOES CCOR-1. No source has been found for this CME.

This CME is visible to the south/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the southeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. There are no clear sources observed on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the south/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the southeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to a small filament eruption centered near S45W25 as seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery which begins to lift off around 2026-11-14T03:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap starting at 2026-11-14T13:23Z. The source is likely far-sided as there are no corresponding source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

cmes.note: A loop CME seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. It overlaps with the 2026-11-14T14:00Z CME and seems faster than it, so it possibly catches up with it. No clear source has been found for this CME, so it is likely far-sided.

Bright CME with a narrower brighter bulk and a wider fainter shock seen to the NE in CCOR-1. Its source is an elongated, fast developing filament eruption from close to the NE limb ~(N17E70) starting at 2026-11-14T21:17Z and seemingly deflecting northward. There is an associated relatively long duration C2.8 flare originating near AR 14579 (N17E72) and peaking at 2026-11-14T21:27Z, as well as a type II burst. The long erupting filament is best seen in GOES SUVI 304/284 imagery but also seen in SDO AIA 304/131/171, with an EUV wave seen clearly in AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate preliminary analysis based on the location of the source eruption (N17E70) and on early GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C3 imagery.

Speculative shock analysis based on the shape of the faint fuzzy shock in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. The CME is not currently seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph because of the large data gap starting at 2026-11-17:53Z.
Updated bulk measurement based on the source location using later frames of SOHO LASCO C3 imagery.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the west in STEREO A COR2 imagery only. The source is likely far-sided as there are no corresponding source signatures on the Earth or STEREO-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 161 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely related to a far-sided filament eruption observed over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/304 and GOES SUVI 171/284/304 imagery which lifts-off around 2026-11-15T08:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no corresponding source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption centered at approximately S15W155 as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-15T18:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source longitude.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to a C2.3 flare from Active Region 14578 (S12W50) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-16T11:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to an eruption from Active Region 14578 (S12W51) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-16T14:54Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to a C2.2 flare and eruption from Active Region 14578 (S12W52) as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-16T16:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-11-16T21:48Z. It is also seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1. The CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C3, or in later frames in SOHO LASCO C2 in real time due to data gaps. The source of this CME is most likely an eruption from AR 14578 (S12W58) beginning around 2026-11-16T21:18Z best seen in SDO AIA 304 as westward directed ejecta.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on probable source location.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to a C2.0 flare and eruption from Active Region 14578 (S12W61) seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-17T04:51Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and to the north in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided and related to a filament eruption visible over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171/304 and GOES SUVI 171/284/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-17T06:20Z. An opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb at this time in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171/284 imagery as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is an M1.1 flare and eruption from Active Region 14578 (S12W68) seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery starting around 2026-11-17T15:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the source longitude.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the NW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-11-17T19:53Z. It is also seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is likely far-sided and possibly related to some very faint field line movement seen well beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-11-17T18:00Z. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmes.note: Narrow CME first seen to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-11-17T20:30Z. It is also seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source is likely related to a filament eruption from AR 14579 (N15E36) beginning around 2026-11-17T19:01Z best seen in SDO AIA 304. The ejecta appears to be directed northeastward.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 as well as on visible source location.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-11-17T22:30Z. It is covered by real-time data gaps in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is likely associated with an M1.7 class flare from 14578 (S12W71) which peaked at 2026-11-17T21:39Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131 accompanied by some westward directed ejecta best seen in SDO AIA 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on probable source location.

cmes.note: Narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and faintly in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery and may be obscured by a data gap from 2026-11-17T20:53Z to 2026-11-18T02:38Z. The source is not clear but may be an eruption beyond the NE limb as seen from SDO and GOES. An eruption starting around 2026-11-18T01:40Z can be seen beyond the east limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery, but timing-wise this may not be the best candidate source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cmes.note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is a filament eruption centered around N10W80. The eruption starts around 2026-11-18T00:52Z as seen as moving field lines near the west limb in GOES SUVI 284/304 and SDO AIA 193 imagery. Post-eruption dimming can also be seen in STEREO A EUV 195 following a data gap from 2026-11-17T21:05Z to 2026-11-18T01:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmes.note: Narrow CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is not found in available EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.

cmes.note: This CME is visible to the SW in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-11-18T07:53Z to 2026-11-18T11:09Z. The CME may also be visible to the west in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3, but is overlapping in the field of view with the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2026-11-18T02:00Z. The source may be part of the eruption seen near disk center in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery, potentially centered around S05W90 starting around 2026-11-18T03:55Z with moving field lines and minor dimming observed.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. The CME front is notably distorted in the COR2 field-of-view, as such the fit encompasses the matching width from CCOR-1 and tracks the edges of the front in COR2, finding a good fit around W80-W90, better closer to W90.

cmes.note: Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-18T16:00Z. This CME fades before exiting the field-of-view in C2 and is there for not visible in other coronagraphs. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen originating from Active Region 14581 (S10E56) beginning at approx. 20206-11-18T10:54Z as seen as dimming and field line opening in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2.

cmes.note: CME first seen to the SW by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-11-18T21:15Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2 due to a data gap from 2026-11-18T19:00Z to 2026-11-18T23:12Z, or STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-18T16:38Z. The source of this event is likely beyond the SW limb and can be seen as field line movement/opening in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-11-18T19:48Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky due to source beyond the limb and lack of STEREO A COR2 imagery to triangulate
